sources.title: Meta Andromeda: Supercharging Advantage+ automation with the next-gen personalized ads retrieval engine
sections: intro: retrieval selects from tens of millions of candidates to a few thousand
Challenges and opportunities…: generative-AI creative tools expected to grow the number of ad creatives significantly
keyFindings: Andromeda is the retrieval stage of Meta's multi-stage ads recommendation system; ranking models decide the final ads.
Meta expects the number of ad creatives to grow significantly because of generative-AI creative tools.
limitations: Describes infrastructure, not creative guidelines; gives no rule about what a good creative looks like.
Says nothing about how a single small advertiser's creative is scored.
sources.productUse: Context only. Forbids any claim that Adlytic Check knows or predicts how Andromeda treats an ad.

sources.title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
sections: Abstract
1 Introduction
keyFindings: 15 US advertising RCTs at Facebook (500M user-experiment observations, 1.6B impressions).
Observational methods often fail to reproduce the experimental effects, even with extensive demographic and behavioural controls.
limitations: US campaigns from 2015; measures campaign effects, not creative quality.
Read: abstract and introduction of the author-hosted 2018 manuscript, not the typeset journal article.
sources.productUse: Basis for the hard rule that a content review cannot predict sales/CTR, and for recommending a randomized A/B test when the owner wants to know which version works.

sources.title: Capture Attention with Updated Features for Video Ads
sections: paragraph on mobile feed viewing without sound
keyFindings: Most video ads in mobile feed are viewed without sound, so the message should be expressed visually.
Captions, logos and products help communicate the message in silence.
limitations: Publisher blocks automated fetching (HTTP 400 from CI); only a search excerpt was read.
Older post; publication date not verified; Reels audio habits may differ.
sources.productUse: Video rule: the core message must be understandable with sound off (on-screen text/captions).

sources.title: Reels ad safe zones (Meta Ads Guide, as reported by third-party spec guides)
sections: Reels 9:16 margins
keyFindings: Most frequently reported guidance for 9:16 Reels ads: keep text, logos and key elements out of roughly the top 14%, bottom 35% and ~6% of each side.
Secondary sources disagree on the bottom margin (20%–40%) and recommend Meta's safe-zone preview in Ads Manager.
limitations: Meta's own page could not be read; numbers differ between guides; treat as a heuristic only.
sources.productUse: Inference-only rule for vertical (9:16) media: warn that text near the bottom may be covered, and point to the Ads Manager preview as the authority.

sources.title: Meta's former 20% image-text rule and current recommendation
sources.publisher: Social Media Today; Jon Loomer Digital (reporting Meta Help Center wording)
sections: report of the 2020 policy change
keyFindings: Meta stopped penalizing ads with more image text in delivery (2020).
Help Center wording still recommends keeping image text light ("less than 20%").
limitations: A recommendation, not an enforced rule; current Help Center wording not verified first-hand.
sources.productUse: Weak-evidence rule: crowded text is flagged for readability, never as a delivery penalty.

sources.title: Meta Experiments: A/B test and Conversion Lift (Ads Manager)
sources.publisher: Meta (reported by Jon Loomer Digital; Triple Whale)
sections: Experiments tool: A/B test with 2–5 variations
Conversion Lift: randomized test vs control holdout
keyFindings: Ads Manager's Experiments tool runs A/B tests between 2–5 variations.
Conversion Lift compares a test group with a randomized control group that is not shown the ads.
limitations: Meta Help Center pages block automated fetching; descriptions come from practitioners.
sources.productUse: When owners ask which variant is better, recommend testing the alternate openings with Meta's A/B test instead of trusting a predicted winner.

sources.title: YouTube ABCDs: Video ad best practices
sections: intro: collaboration with Ipsos; Nielsen and Kantar as independent reviewers
"On average, the ABCDs deliver a 30% lift in short-term sales likelihood and a 17% lift in long-term brand contribution"
keyFindings: Four principles: Attention/Attract, Branding/Brand, Connection/Connect, Direction/Direct (ask for action).
Vendor-reported association with short-term sales likelihood (Google/Kantar).
limitations: Vendor research on YouTube, not Meta; correlational association reported by the platform owner.
sources.productUse: Supports the opening (attention), brand presence and clear call-to-action dimensions as checks — never as performance promises.

sources.title: Attention Capture and Transfer in Advertising: Brand, Pictorial, and Text-Size Effects
sections: Abstract (via indexing service and University of Michigan press release)
keyFindings: Eye-tracking of 3,600+ consumers on 1,363 print ads: pictorial captures attention regardless of size; attention to text depends on text surface size.
limitations: Print magazines, 2004; later studies did not always replicate the size interactions (Frontiers in Psychology 2013 review).
sources.productUse: Supports: product picture is the first thing seen; key words must be large enough to be read.

sources.title: Moment-to-Moment Optimal Branding in TV Commercials: Preventing Avoidance by Pulsing
sections: Abstract
keyFindings: 31 commercials, ~2,000 participants: dispersed attention predicts zapping; brief, repeated brand appearances (pulsing) reduced avoidance versus one long brand exposure.
limitations: TV commercials, not mobile feeds; effect sizes reported in trade press were not verified.
sources.productUse: Video: suggest showing the shop/brand briefly more than once rather than one long logo slate (inference).

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 — 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
sections: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum): 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large-scale text
keyFindings: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) to be readable by people with moderately low vision.
limitations: Written for web text, not ad images; the model estimates contrast visually and cannot measure it exactly.
sources.productUse: Legibility rule: low contrast between text and background is a readability problem (inference from the image).

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers — Limits
sections: Account plan limits (CPU 10 ms Free / up to 5 min Paid; memory 128 MB; subrequests 50 Free)
Request body size by Cloudflare plan (100 MB Free/Pro)
keyFindings: Workers have 128 MB memory and, on the Free plan, 10 ms CPU per request — unsuitable for video decoding.
limitations: Limits change; re-check before scaling.
sources.productUse: Architecture: no ffmpeg/decoding in the Worker; video frames and audio are extracted in the browser.

sources.title: Workers AI — whisper-large-v3-turbo model page and Workers AI pricing
sections: Model info: $0.000513 per audio minute; parameters language, vad_filter, no_speech_threshold
Pricing: 10,000 Neurons/day free on Free and Paid plans; $0.011 / 1,000 Neurons
keyFindings: Speech recognition with segment timestamps is available as a Worker binding.
A 60-second clip costs about $0.0005.
limitations: Arabic dialect accuracy not documented; must be measured on fixtures.
sources.productUse: Video audio transcription (speech_transcribed / no_audio / silence / unavailable).

sources.title: Cloudflare Queues limits, Workflows limits, Containers pricing
sections: Queues: 128 KB message, 15 min consumer wall time
Workflows: 1 MiB step result / event payload; Free plan 10 ms CPU per step
Containers: Workers Paid only (no Free tier)
keyFindings: Containers (the only place ffmpeg could run) require Workers Paid; Queue messages are capped at 128 KB, so media must live elsewhere.
limitations: Account plan of this deployment is not visible from the session.
sources.productUse: Decision D-006: avoid Containers for V2 video; keep the synchronous path within one request.

sources.title: R2 presigned URLs
sections: presigned PUT/GET with expiry
keyFindings: Presigned URLs grant time-limited upload/download without making a bucket public.
limitations: Requires S3 API credentials stored as Worker secrets.
sources.productUse: Roadmap option for larger uploads; not needed while frames are extracted client-side.

sources.title: OpenID Connect (Google Identity)
sections: Create an anti-forgery state token
Validating an ID token (iss, aud, exp, nonce)
email_verified claim
keyFindings: Use a state token against CSRF; validate iss/aud/exp; use sub as the stable user identifier.
sources.productUse: Identity: Google OIDC with state, nonce and PKCE; account key = issuer + sub.

sources.title: RFC 9700 — Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sections: 2.1.1 Authorization Code Grant (PKCE, CSRF)
4.1 Insufficient Redirect URI Validation (exact string matching)
keyFindings: Clients use PKCE; redirect URIs are matched exactly; one-time CSRF protection via state or PKCE.
sources.productUse: Identity implementation checklist.

sources.title: Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sections: Case 2: application can send requests to any external IP/domain — validate resolved IPs, block private/link-local/IPv6 mapped ranges, disable redirect following, DNS rebinding
keyFindings: Validate the destination after DNS resolution, re-check on every redirect, and block internal ranges in IPv4 and IPv6.
sources.productUse: Direct-file link import controls.

sources.title: ZainCash Payment Gateway API Documentation v2
sections: POST /oauth2/token (client credentials)
POST /api/v2/payment-gateway/transaction/init
GET /api/v2/payment-gateway/transaction/inquiry/{transactionId} (scope payment:read)
Redirect with JWT token to successUrl/failureUrl
Webhook: source of truth, production only, registered by the business team
UAT base URL https://pg-api-uat.zaincash.iq
keyFindings: v2 uses OAuth2 client credentials; webhook is the source of truth; inquiry is the fallback; webhook is not available in UAT.
limitations: Site returns a Cloudflare challenge to automated fetches (403 from CI); webhook signature scheme and minimum amount not confirmed.
sources.productUse: Payment adapter design; anything unconfirmed is verified by inquiry, never trusted from the redirect.

sources.title: ZainCash business wallets — fees table
sections: Merchant payment gateway fee by wallet type
keyFindings: Small Projects wallet: 1% with a minimum of 500 IQD per gateway payment (30M IQD monthly limit).
Merchant and Company/NGO wallets: 0.6% with a minimum of 150 IQD.
limitations: Page blocks automated fetching; search indexer reported the page as ~621 days old; negotiated terms may differ.
sources.productUse: Unit economics: a single 500 IQD purchase is uneconomic on a Small Projects wallet; bundles are shown explicitly.

sources.title: Instagram Platform: oEmbed, Meta oEmbed Read feature, Business Discovery
sections: oEmbed: App Access Token server-side; Meta oEmbed Read requires App Review
oEmbed Read: thumbnail_url/author fields deprecated (Nov 3 2025)
Business Discovery: Facebook User token with instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights, pages_read_engagement; only Business/Creator accounts
keyFindings: Official access to another account's post media requires an approved Meta app and user authorization; oEmbed no longer returns thumbnails.
limitations: developers.facebook.com blocks automated fetching (400 from CI); a June 2026 tokenless-oEmbed change is reported only by a secondary blog and is unverified.
sources.productUse: Link support matrix: Instagram/Facebook links are AUTH_REQUIRED or UNSUPPORTED; no scraping.

sources.title: MDN — BaseAudioContext.decodeAudioData() and HTMLVideoElement.requestVideoFrameCallback()
sections: decodeAudioData: decodes audio from a media file's ArrayBuffer
requestVideoFrameCallback: per-frame callback with mediaTime
keyFindings: Browsers can decode a video's audio track and draw frames to a canvas without server-side ffmpeg.
limitations: Codec support differs by browser; must be tested in Chromium and WebKit.
sources.productUse: Client-side video frame and audio extraction.

sources.title: Adlytic product hypotheses (internal, not external evidence)
sections: industry checklists of commonly missing details; Iraqi messaging-first ordering habits
keyFindings: Hypothesis: shop owners selling through Instagram/WhatsApp lose orders when price, sizes or ordering method are missing.
limitations: Not externally validated; labelled as hypothesis wherever used.
sources.productUse: Missing-details suggestions only, never presented as research findings.
